package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a critical vulnerability (CVE-2024-4367) that allows arbitrary JavaScript code execution when rendering malicious PDF files. This enables attackers to execute code in the context of the application or browser using PDF.js, leading to potential compromise of user data and system integrity.

execution_context.file_location: core font rendering logic (JavaScript source of pdf.js)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code dynamically constructs a JavaScript function from PDF font rendering commands (cmds) using the Function constructor, which executes in the context of the PDF viewer. If an attacker controls the cmds array (via PDF metadata such as FontMatrix), they can inject arbitrary JavaScript code, leading to code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dynamically generating and executing code from untrusted input (PDF metadata) is highly dangerous, as it allows attackers to inject and run arbitrary code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal PDF rendering should never execute arbitrary JavaScript from document metadata. The use of Function with attacker-controlled input is a severe violation of secure coding practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic code generation for performance optimization is sometimes used in trusted, internal contexts, but never with untrusted user input.
key_indicators: Use of new Function with attacker-controlled input
Direct injection of PDF metadata into executable code
No sanitization or validation of cmds array

execution_context.file_location: PDF metadata (FontMatrix array in PDF file)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malicious FontMatrix value is parsed and injected into the dynamically generated JavaScript function, breaking out of the intended syntax and executing arbitrary JavaScript (e.g., alert('foobar')).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Embedding JavaScript payloads in PDF metadata to break out of data context and execute code is a classic injection attack.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: FontMatrix should only contain numeric transformation values, not executable code or strings.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; FontMatrix should never contain JavaScript.
key_indicators: Presence of JavaScript code in PDF metadata
Use of special characters to break out of data context

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious PDF with a FontMatrix containing injected JavaScript code.
attack_chain.leads_to: PDF is opened in a vulnerable PDF.js viewer.

attack_chain.action: PDF.js parses the PDF and passes the malicious FontMatrix value into the font rendering logic.
attack_chain.leads_to: Dynamic JavaScript function is constructed with attacker-controlled code.

attack_chain.action: The dynamically generated function executes the injected JavaScript code in the context of the viewer.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code execution (e.g., alert, data exfiltration, further exploitation).

behavioral_signatures: Dynamic use of Function or eval with PDF-derived input
Execution of JavaScript code from PDF metadata fields
Unexpected JavaScript execution during PDF rendering
file_indicators: PDF files with non-numeric or suspicious values in FontMatrix
Presence of special characters or JavaScript code in PDF metadata
network_indicators: Unexpected outbound requests triggered by PDF rendering
Connections to attacker-controlled domains after opening a PDF
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for use of the Function constructor or eval in PDF.js code paths, especially where input is derived from PDF metadata. Scan PDF files for non-numeric values or suspicious strings in FontMatrix and other metadata fields. Implement content security policies to block eval and Function usage. Alert on unexpected JavaScript execution or network activity triggered by PDF rendering.
